relevance_note: Single case report of a girl with a GFAP variant diagnosed with Alexander disease: "The patient was eventually diagnosed with Alexander's disease."
method_note: Read the whole paper (case report plus literature review; no tables, no supplement). Output assembled with a short Python script from my reading; every span checked verbatim by script. Scope: the index patient; both parents (tested, wild-type) as 'parent of patient' and 'parent of patient 2' (sex not stated); the sister ('currently healthy') was neither tested nor affected, so she gets no row. Previously published people from the Discussion with individual-level facts were included: Zardadi et al. (28) patient (R88; area postrema-like syndrome; atonic seizures; prednisolone), an unreferenced 'patient with an R88C mutation with microcephaly ... reported in India' (unnamed person 1; 'India' is where the report came from, not recorded as origin), and the Sechi et al. (66) 'adult patient' with ataxia and dysarthria (no variant printed, so no variant row). Disease labels for the ref (28) and ref (66) patients are taken from the reference-list titles. Left out: the homozygous Taiwanese report (25) (no individual-level detail beyond the variant class), novel variants listed from refs 29-32 (no person described), and cases cited only as groups (refs 11, 12, 27, 34). Index patient: rsID 'RS: 61622935' in Figure 3 legend not recorded in any field; protein change given only in words ('88th amino acid change from arginine to cysteine') and as R88/R88C in the Discussion, so protein_hgvs is null; variant type not stated, left not reported. Inheritance recorded de novo because both parents were tested and wild-type (the paper does not use the word 'de novo' for this patient). Functional evidence is a literature statement on R88C astrocytes (ref 26), not on this patient's cells. Onset taken as the first convulsion at 1 year 7 months; head drop began 5 months before admission at age 4. 'neck strength (–)' was not recorded (meaning of the sign unclear). 'Babinski sign (–)' recorded excluded. Normal findings converted per D-27 (e.g. 'limb muscle tone normal' -> abnormal limb muscle tone excluded; normal coordination tests -> ataxia excluded). General negatives ('no brainstem symptoms or motor abnormalities', 'No abnormal positive neurological signs', biochemical examination) recorded as worded, without excluding narrower checklist items. Macrocephaly excluded from head circumference at the 15th percentile. Cerebral white matter abnormality checklist marked observed from the paraventricular abnormal signals; periventricular rim left not reported. No contradictions found.
